statements.text: The Region plans $847.6 million of water supply capital work from 2026 to 2035, with $73.5 million in 2027.
$487.9 million of that is for upgrades, expansion and new facilities.
Development charges on new building pay $311.9 million of it, and water rates pay $525.4 million through the Water Capital Reserve.
Running the water supply system costs $47.9 million in 2026, before paying for capital.
The Region says its water assets need $54.7 million a year of renewal, but the 10-year plan invests $31.5 million a year, a gap of $23.2 million a year.

assumptions.label: Years counted
assumptions.why: 25 years (2026–2050) runs close to the strategy's 2051 horizon. Pipes, wells and plants last longer, so their renewal keeps going after that.

assumptions.label: Discount rate
assumptions.why: At 0% every year's dollar counts the same. A higher rate counts future dollars for less, as many public-sector cost studies do (3% is common).

assumptions.label: Yearly running cost
assumptions.why: The 2026 operating budget, held flat in today's dollars. New wells or sources chosen by the strategy will add running costs that are not published yet.

assumptions.label: Renewal counted
assumptions.why: 2026–2035: the $23.2 million a year the Region says is missing from renewal. After 2035: the full $54.7 million a year need, assuming it stays at today's level. Slide to 0 to count only what is budgeted.

assumptions.label: Capital cost overrun
assumptions.why: Construction prices can rise faster than budgets. Slide to see what an overrun on the capital program adds.

assumptions.label: Households sharing the cost
assumptions.why: 222,426 households lived in Waterloo Region at the 2021 Census (Statistics Canada). There are more now. Businesses pay too, so this is a rough share per home, not a bill.

method: Lifecycle cost = capital in the years it is spent + operating and maintenance in each year of service + renewals in the years they fall + emissions × carbon price (none counted here), over the years shown, in today's dollars, undiscounted unless a discount rate is set. Built in code by lenses/cost from figures whose quotes were checked on their pages; everything else is a labelled assumption.
inputNotes: Capital: the budget book's yearly totals for 2026–2030 (cited) and its 2031–2035 subtotal spread evenly (assumption). 2026 includes earlier approvals not yet spent.
No capital after 2035 is counted: the strategy's new sources will add to it, and their costs are not published.
Operating: the 2026 operating subtotal (cited), held flat in today's dollars (assumption). Maintenance is inside it.

Renewal: the unfunded gap ($23.2 million a year, cited) for 2026–2035, then the full need ($54.7 million a year, cited) after the 10-year plan ends (assumption). The gap report's 'Water' line covers the Region's water assets, which may include more than water supply.
Emissions are not counted: no document gives the water system's emissions.
unknowns: The cost of each shortlisted water source option: not published until the strategy's evaluation is released.
How water rates would change to pay for the preferred option.
summary:
LIFECYCLE COST over 25 years (2026-2050), service from 2026, discount rate 0.0%, today's dollars:
- Capital $847.6 million (27%)
- Operating $1.20 billion (39%)
- Maintenance $0 (0%)
- Renewal $1.05 billion (34%)
- Environmental (emissions x carbon price) $0 (0%)
- Lifecycle total $3.10 billion; the upfront price is 27% of it.
- Per household (222,426 households): $13,924 over the period, about $557 a year.
